result.title: A Finite-Rate Selection Law for Annealed Gibbs Sampling
result.comment: 12 pages, 2 figures, 4 tables. Accepted at DynaFront2026: Dynamics at the Frontiers of Optimization, Sampling, and Games; NeurIPS 2026 Workshop
result.summary: Annealed Gibbs sampling samples a multimodal model by redrawing one variable at a time from its conditional distribution as the temperature falls from a high value, where the distribution is broad, to the target temperature. Each run ends in a single mode, and unbiased Monte Carlo estimates require the runs to end in each mode in proportion to its probability under the model. At a finite cooling rate this can fail. We measure the error by $c$, the fraction of the model's log-odds between two modes that the samples retain. In the Curie--Weiss model, where a weak external field favors one of two modes, each run selects its mode near the transition at which the modes form, and rarely switches once they have separated. Near the transition, the random fluctuations of the Gibbs updates still outweigh the weak field, which therefore biases the choice of mode only slightly. Building on the selection probability of Kondepudi and coworkers, we derive a law for $c$ that agrees with an exact computation to within $2\%$ on nine linear cooling ramps. For the Hopfield model, whose modes are stored patterns and their negatives, we derive a factor by which competition among patterns raises $c$. The $c$ measured over random pattern sets lies within $3$--$6\%$ of its prediction, but single pattern sets depart from it, contrary to its derivation.

AI.brief_summary: 该文研究退火 Gibbs 采样在有限降温速率下模式选择比例失衡的问题，在 Curie–Weiss 与 Hopfield 模型中推导并验证一个刻画模式概率保留程度的有限速率选择律。
